name: VEED
tagline: Browser video editing, recording, subtitles, avatars, and collaboration

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 10 video minutes/month; 2 auto-subtitle minutes/month; 720p watermarked exports; 1 AI-avatar trial
tiers.notes: Official VEED comparison copy is inconsistent about whether the 10-minute figure is a monthly pool or maximum video length.

tiers.name: Lite
tiers.limits: 2 video hours/month; 12 auto-subtitle hours/month; 16 AI-avatar minutes/month; 1080p watermark-free exports
tiers.notes: The current official comparison page calls this Lite, while newer feature-help pages refer to an entry paid tier as Creator.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 5 video hours/month; 20 AI-avatar minutes/month; 20 translation minutes/month; 4K exports
tiers.notes: The official comparison page reports 20 auto-subtitle minutes/month here, which appears inconsistent with Lite's 12 hours; retained as a source conflict rather than treated as reliable.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats, credits, security, onboarding and support

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 video minutes/month, 2 auto-subtitle minutes/month, 720p watermarked exports and 1 AI-avatar trial
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual prices shown as effective monthly rates; monthly billing is unavailable in India, where only annual plans are offered
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI generation uses credits that expire at the end of the billing period; collaborator seats are billed; plan names and at least one subtitle allowance conflict across VEED's own current pages.

verdictSummary: The visible online video editor loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. VEED earns its keep through media pipeline, hosting, distribution, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local online video editor workflow that imports user-owned media, applies the core edit or transformation, previews it, and exports a standard file.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: optional model or API key in .env
whatYouLose: production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates
whyPeopleStillPay: VEED: People pay to avoid codec failures, upload limits, rendering surprises, lost recordings, and distribution chores.
ongoingBurden: Maintain codecs, media probing, resumable processing, storage cleanup, exports, device permissions, and performance.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express
alternatives.desc: Browser editing, recording, captions and graphics without a watermark; avatars and team machinery stay elsewhere.

alternatives.name: Clipchamp
alternatives.desc: A capable browser editor and recorder with free 1080p exports; collaboration and avatars are thinner.

rejectedAlternatives.name: OpenCut
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The famous answer is between codebases: classic is archived and the replacement is still a rewrite.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of VEED is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for VEED, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + FFmpeg + React.
Primary job: Build a local online video editor workflow that imports user-owned media, applies the core edit or transformation, previews it, and exports a standard file.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates; hosted recording reliability; large-scale rendering.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
